{
  "research_question": "How do different stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance across five key metrics: Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform one-way ANOVA for each response variable with Stim Paradigm as the independent factor",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use logistic regression or chi-square test instead of standard ANOVA",
    "For Path Efficiency and AD, assess normality and consider transformations if needed before ANOVA",
    "Use robust ANOVA methods if heteroscedasticity is detected across groups"
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check normality of residuals using Shapiro-Wilk test for each ANOVA",
    "Assess homogeneity of variances using Levene's test",
    "Examine residual plots for patterns indicating violations",
    "For Success variable, assess model fit and overdispersion in logistic regression",
    "Verify independence assumption through experimental design review"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA is significant (p<0.05), perform Tukey HSD tests for pairwise comparisons",
    "For logistic regression of Success, use post-hoc contrasts with multiple comparison adjustment",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., Cohen's d, odds ratios) alongside p-values",
    "Use Bonferroni or FDR correction for multiple testing across all response variables"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows superior performance across most metrics",
    "Sham condition expected to show poorest navigation performance",
    "Visual-only paradigms (Dim and Bright) may show intermediate performance",
    "ICMS Only may show better performance than visual-only but worse than Combined",
    "Significant differences in angular dispersion (AD) between active stimulation and sham"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Uneven group sizes (Combined: 48,846 vs. Bright Visual Only: 3,323) may affect power",
    "Success variable is binary, requiring specialized analysis methods",
    "Potential non-normality in Path Efficiency and AD based on summary statistics",
    "No information about within-mouse correlations or repeated measures structure",
    "Summary-only view prevents examination of individual trial characteristics"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Perform mixed-effects modeling to account for mouse-level variability and repeated measures structure, using the full trial-level data rather than summary statistics"
}
